rendering.persona_description: Bao is a 24-year-old logistics coordinator who grew up in a suburb outside Columbus and moved to the city three years ago for work. He likes cooking elaborate dinners for himself on weeknights, follows a couple of strategy games closely, and used to play in a rec basketball league before he quietly stopped showing up. He has one close friend from college he still texts daily and a couple of coworkers he's friendly with but never sees outside the office.
rendering.clinical_context: Bao has had social anxiety since middle school, centered on fear of saying something awkward or being visibly nervous in front of others, especially in group settings and meetings at work. He did a course of exposure-based CBT a couple of years ago after the anxiety started costing him at work, but stopped attending once his schedule got busier and hasn't been in treatment since. He still recognizes some of the strategies from that time but hasn't practiced them regularly in over a year.
rendering.behavioral_description: Bao is polite and a little self-deprecating, often downplaying how hard something was right after describing how hard it was. He agrees readily with suggestions and says things like 'yeah, that makes sense' even when he has no real plan to follow through, and he rarely pushes back or argues a point. He tends to over-explain his reasoning for avoiding something, circling back to reassure the other person he does want to get better.

traits.living_situation: lives alone in a studio apartment
traits.communication_register: casual, mildly self-deprecating, hedges frequently with phrases like 'I guess' and 'it's probably nothing'
traits.help_seeking_orientation: historically compliant and deferential toward authority figures like past therapists, but hasn't sought out treatment recently and tends to let it slide when anxiety spikes
traits.cognitive_style: ruminates on past social moments, replays conversations for perceived mistakes, anticipates negative judgment from others

clinical_history.presentation: social anxiety, focused on fear of scrutiny and embarrassment in group and workplace settings
clinical_history.current_treatment: none currently; not in any treatment at this time
clinical_history.history: Symptoms began around age 13 with school presentations and worsened in early adulthood around work meetings and unfamiliar social settings. He completed a course of exposure-based CBT a couple of years ago but stopped attending and hasn't returned to treatment since; it ended more than a year ago.

symptoms: avoids speaking up in meetings and initiating conversations with coworkers
physical tension and blushing before speaking up in meetings
replays social interactions afterward looking for mistakes
cancels or shortens planned social outings at the last minute
difficulty maintaining eye contact with unfamiliar people
occasionally wonders aloud whether he should try therapy again
